judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening description contains an outright mechanical garble ("promotions, discounts, coupons, vouchers, ordeals" for "or deals") and an open-ended definition sweeping in "any other products and services offered by Angie's List at any time" as the "Service", so the reach of the central defined term is uncertain; the promise that Angie's List "provides reviews and ratings ... to allow you ... to read about the experiences other users have had" is exactly the sort of introductory description a member would read as a substantive undertaking. Both the catch-all definition and the descriptive representation give a court something to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This introductory description points the opposite way from Section 13 (passive conduit; no guarantee of accuracy or integrity of Content) and Section 24 (no warranty that results will be accurate or reliable), and its statement that "You will receive notice if modifications to the Agreement are made" sits against Section 19, which makes modifications "effective immediately upon being posted". That is a classic recital-versus-operative-text tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[B]ased upon the actual first-hand experiences other users have had" is the contract's core descriptive representation and is genuinely open to two readings — a mere description of the source of raw reviews, or an affirmative promise that the ratings presented are unmanipulated and untainted by anything else. A member and the company could plainly read "based upon" differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with Section 13's "passive conduit" disclaimer and Section 24's express disclaimer that results obtained from the Service will be "accurate or reliable", and with Section 20's reservation of unpublished practices governing retention and display of ratings. Whether Section 1 survives those disclaimers is precisely a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]n good standing" is undefined and its boundary cannot be applied, and the text carries a mechanical corruption ("within cone-year period") that obscures the redemption window for Redeemable Benefits. The reservation to "modify the Plans at any time and in its sole discretion" also leaves what a member actually bought indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The listed Premium benefit "Access to Angie's List's Complaint Resolution Process" is contradicted by Section 11, which makes participation "at Angie's List's sole discretion" with a right to reject "for any reason", and the unilateral right to modify Plans sits against Section 6's fixed Membership Fee mechanics. That is a real internal tension worth naming.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional accuracy-of-registration-information covenant; "true, accurate, current and complete" is standard and administrable. Nothing here has two competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Section 16(F) and (T) (no impersonation, one account) and Section 26(b) (indemnity for inaccurate information). No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One flat sentence with a numeric threshold; nothing vague or mistaken. Definite terms are low risk however important.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section 16(A) ("are above the age of eighteen (18)") without contradiction. Checked and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Membership in the Service is void where prohibited" is a bare six-word phrase whose operative content — prohibited by what, where, and with what consequence for fees already paid — cannot be applied from the words. Short, wholly undefined phrases of this kind are exactly the vagueness the category targets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument (including Section 18 Term and Termination and Section 30 Governing Law) explains what happens when membership is "void", but neither does anything contradict it. The gap is more textual than relational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A locating reference to an external privacy policy; no operative promise and no ambiguous term within it. Low intrinsic risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the linked privacy policy is incorporated is left unresolved between the preamble ("terms and conditions in, and linked to, this Membership Agreement") and Section 29's entire-agreement clause, and Section 15 says users have no obligation to keep health information confidential. That is a modest but genuine relational uncertainty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "Membership Fee" as the amount charged "not including any promotions or discounts that may have been applied" is genuinely ambiguous about what a renewal will cost, and the reserved right to modify fees "at any time" leaves the price term open. The all-caps auto-renewal sentence is otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises an opt-out "AS PROVIDED BELOW", but nothing below describes an opt-out feature — only the cancellation procedure in CANCELING YOUR SUBSCRIPTION — so the cross-reference fails on the face of the instrument. That dangling reference is a concrete whole-instrument defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]n or about Your expiration date" and "standard renewal practices then in effect (which may be modified from time to time)" leave both the timing and the substance of renewal indeterminate. Those are namable vague terms in a billing provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "on or about" renewal date cannot be reconciled cleanly with the cancellation deadline of 5:00 p.m. on "the business day prior to Your scheduled renewal payment date", and it also depends on the opt-out that Section 6 promises but never supplies. A real fit problem, though a modest one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same drafting as the monthly provision: "on or about Your expiration date" and renewal at a fee that "MAY BE MODIFIED AS PROVIDED ABOVE" leave the renewal price and date uncertain. Namable, if commonplace, vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with the cancellation-deadline provision and with the never-described opt-out referenced in Section 6, creating the same unresolved timing question. Checked against CANCELING YOUR SUBSCRIPTION and the Membership Renewals paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "You formerly had to option to purchase access" is a plain mechanical error, and the paragraph is written in a tense that leaves it unclear whether the Additional List feature has any continuing operation. The defined "primary" subscription is introduced but never used to any effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6 elsewhere charges "Additional List Fees" and the Membership Renewals paragraph provides for renewing "the Additional List", so the past-tense abolition here sits awkwardly with two live provisions. That is a specific internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph conditions renewal on having "received a free offer", a category never defined, and then states flatly that "[a]ll existing memberships will be renewed", which is broader than the conditional sentence preceding it. The two sentences pull against each other within the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to cancelling access "to a particular subscription in accordance with the provisions set forth below", but the cancellation paragraph below addresses only cancellation of the whole subscription. A failed cross-reference of the same kind as the opt-out in Section 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is corrupted ("Down.rcLading") and the upgrade mechanic — you buy "an additional annual subscription", the "first" is upgraded and a "second" begins later — is genuinely hard to apply to any concrete fee calculation. "[R]efund of the difference between Your current Plan and the new Plan" does not say whether it is prorated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The downgrade refund is the only refund promised to a member other than the convenience-termination refund in Section 18, and it sits against Section 1's reservation to modify Plans and pricing at will. Some tension, but no direct contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deadline is expressed by reference to "Your scheduled renewal payment date", a date the contract elsewhere fixes only as "on or about" the expiration date, so the cut-off cannot be computed from the words. "[R]eceived by no later than 5:00 p.m." is otherwise precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires actual receipt, while Section 28 deems notices delivered only on verification or two business days after sending, and it is the provision Section 6 gestures at for an "opt out" that it does not in fact provide. Two identifiable frictions with other operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Saying a portion of the Membership Fee "will be applied towards" the magazine and then that the magazine fee "is not deductible from Your Membership Fee" is close to self-contradictory, and "where applicable" is undefined. A member could reasonably read this as an extra charge or as an allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Plans in Section 1 promise the print magazine only "where available", which is not obviously the same as "where applicable" here, and the flat $6.50 allocation sits against the variable Membership Fee definition in Section 6. Minor but real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A consent and authorization paragraph with a defined term ("Account Updater") applied consistently; the only defect is an OCR artifact ("athird-party") that changes nothing. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly ties itself to "this Agreement and the privacy policy", which is consistent with Section 5 and does not collide with Section 29. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "You agree that You shall not bring any action against Angie's List relating in any way to the Incentives" is a sweeping covenant not to sue whose reach (fraud? statutory consumer claims?) is left to a catch-all phrase; "incorrect, unfit, or unusable in any way" is similarly open-ended. Enough for an ejusdem generis / scope argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with, but does not contradict, Sections 24 and 25, which are the general disclaimer and liability cap; the absolute bar here is broader than the cap in Section 25 but the two can be harmonised. Modest relational risk only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The household definition is expressly supplied ("anyone who currently shares with You the address You registered"), which removes the obvious vagueness. Straightforward allocation of responsibility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Section 16(T) (one account per person) and Section 9's personal-use licence; the household-sharing permission coexists with those without contradiction. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ccess, reproduce, duplicate, copy, sell, re-sell, visit or otherwise exploit for any commercial, educational, or any other non-personal purpose" pairs specifics with a catch-all, and the inclusion of "visit" makes the prohibited conduct hard to bound; "personal purchase decisions" is also undefined. That is a genuine list-scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is largely mirrored by Section 16(P) and (Q), but Section 16(Q) is itself garbled and the two grants of licence differ in wording, leaving which controls unclear. Modest relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence ("to allow the Service Provider to discuss the issue with"), and "active, qualifying Plan", "reasonable timeframe" and "a counteroffer that You find acceptable" are each undefined. There is plenty here for a court to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 lists "Access to Angie's List's Complaint Resolution Process" as a purchased Premium Plan benefit, yet this section makes participation "at Angie's List's sole discretion" with a right to reject "for any reason" — a direct clash between a promised benefit and a discretionary one. That is the strongest internal conflict in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimer of ownership followed by an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable licence and a right to prohibit others' use is broad but internally coherent and carefully enumerated. The defined term "Content" is supplied here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section 16(R), which grants a licence in slightly different terms, and it must be read with Section 18's statement that termination "may include the deletion of the Content"; the perpetual licence survives under Section 31. Overlap rather than contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]imply acts as a passive conduit" is a characterisation, not a defined term, and its reach is contestable given the same document's reserved right to review and delete Content; "bear all risks" is broad. A court could readily be asked what "passive conduit" means here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points the opposite way from Section 1's representation that ratings are based on users' actual first-hand experiences and from Section 20's reservation of unpublished practices governing retention and display, and it is cross-referenced by Sections 11, 14 and 15. That is a live whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, repetitive disclaimer whose repeated parenthetical ("which includes, but is not limited to, health care and wellness providers") is belt-and-braces rather than ambiguous; "available or unavailable" is odd but not two-sided in meaning. Mostly definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly preserved by Sections 11 and 31 and reinforced by Sections 24 and 25, and it does not obviously contradict Section 1's description of the ratings' source, though it disclaims responsibility for the very Content Section 1 describes. Some tension, contained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statement that posted health information "will be placing it into the public domain and it will not be protected by any federal or state laws" is a legal characterisation of doubtful accuracy, and "Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement" leaves the exception unidentified. Those are namable soft spots.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanket denial of any confidentiality obligation sits against the privacy policy referenced in Section 5 and against the HIPAA-waiver machinery in Section 11, and it depends on an unspecified carve-out elsewhere in the Agreement. That is a specific fit question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (Q) is missing a word ("not related to Your personal purchasing decisions, the express written consent of Angie's List" — plainly "without"), and (C) and (D) rest on wholly subjective standards ("distasteful", "otherwise objectionable", "thorough and thoughtful") set against enumerated specifics. Both a mechanical error and a list-scope problem are visible on the face of it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its licence grant in (R) duplicates Section 12 in different words, (O) duplicates Section 32's anti-assignment term, and its remedies paragraph ("if damages are ascertainable, seeking damages") sits beside Section 27's liquidated-damages regime. Overlaps that could be argued but no outright contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ustomer information generally is one of the transferred business assets" is descriptive filler, but the consent itself is clear and bounded by "any purpose allowed under this Agreement". Little ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The consent must be read with the privacy policy in Section 5, which is not set out in the instrument, and Section 31 preserves this section after termination. Mild dependency, no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The initial term is left to be "defined in Your membership Plan", a document not reproduced, and the refund trigger — "merely terminates Your account for its convenience" — is an undefined and value-laden phrase. A member and the company could easily differ over whether a termination was "for convenience".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says termination is "by either party in accordance with the terms of this Agreement", but the only member-side exit described anywhere is the cancellation paragraph in Section 6, and the pro rata refund promised here sits against Section 20's disclaimer of liability for discontinuing the Service and Section 25's cap. That is a genuine reconciliation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Modifications are "effective immediately upon being posted" yet the same paragraph says "You will receive notice", without saying whether notice is a condition; "Your continued use" as "conclusive acceptance" is a further contestable term. The unilateral-amendment mechanic is the kind of provision whose bindingness turns on these words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble likewise promises that "You will receive notice if modifications to the Agreement are made" while this section makes posting alone effective, and the recourse offered ("immediately discontinue use") sits against the automatic renewal and cancellation-deadline provisions of Section 6. A specific, locatable inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reservation of "general practices, policies and limits, which may or may not be published" is expressly unascertainable from the document, and the enumerated examples are followed by an open "including without limitation". Both features invite a scope argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A right to discontinue the Service with no liability is difficult to square with Section 18's promise of a pro rata refund on convenience termination and with the paid, plan-specific benefits enumerated in Section 1. That tension is real though arguably harmonisable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences allocating internet-related risk; "inherent in the use of the Internet" is slightly loose but the provision has one plain meaning. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a narrower instance of the disclaimers in Sections 24 and 25 and conflicts with nothing checked. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]reative ideas, suggestions, or materials other than those which we have specifically requested" draws a line the member cannot apply, and "Submissions" is then defined by a list ending in "or other information", a catch-all that could swallow ordinary feedback. That is a namable list-scope defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12 states that Angie's List "does not claim ownership" of Content, while this section takes outright ownership of Submissions, and the boundary between "Content" and "Submissions" is nowhere drawn. That is a concrete conflict worth flagging.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional IP-ownership statement with an enumerated list carved out of user Content; "all other materials" is broad but its residual character is clear. Low intrinsic risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly carves out user-submitted Content and Service Provider Content, aligning with Sections 12 and 13, and survives under Section 31. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence is garbled ("NO RESPONSIBILITY OR LIABILITY FOR THE TIMELINESS, DELETION OF CONTENT OR FAILURE BY THE SERVICE"), and the closing savings clause ("some of the foregoing disclaimers may not apply") leaves which disclaimers survive undetermined. Both are visible on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Disclaiming any warranty that results "WILL BE ACCURATE OR RELIABLE" runs against Section 1's representation that ratings are based on users' actual first-hand experiences, and it is expressly preserved by Sections 11, 14 and 31. This is the disclaimer a member's accuracy claim would collide with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It purports to exclude "DIRECT" damages resulting from "ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT BY ANGIE'S LIST", which read literally leaves the member no remedy at all; the closing savings sentence again leaves the surviving scope undefined. A court asked to enforce it would have to construe how far it goes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanket exclusion cannot easily be reconciled with the very next paragraph's cap on "ANGIE'S LIST'S LIABILITY FOR DAMAGES", with Section 25's final sentence that "ANGIE'S LIST SHALL BE SOLELY LIABLE FOR THE PAYMENT OF ANY DAMAGES TO YOU", or with Section 18's refund obligation. That is a specific whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap is arithmetically precise and its prorating rule is spelled out; the recital that unlimited access "represents a substantial portion of the value" is colour rather than an operative ambiguity. Low intrinsic risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cap presupposes liability that the immediately preceding paragraph purports to exclude altogether, and it sits against Section 18's promise of a pro rata refund of a full term's fees, which would exceed one month. A locatable inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(AS DEFINED HEREIN AND SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATIONS SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION SUFFERED BY YOU" is never closed, so the qualification's reach is genuinely unclear, and "ANY OTHER PARTY INVOLVED IN THE CREDIT CARD PROCESSING PROCESS" is an unbounded catch-all following two specifics. Both a mechanical error and a list-scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its closing statement that "ANGIE'S LIST SHALL BE SOLELY LIABLE FOR THE PAYMENT OF ANY DAMAGES TO YOU" contradicts the opening of Section 25, which says Angie's List "WILL NOT BE LIABLE FOR ANY" damages, and it is the hook for Section 32's third-party-beneficiary sentence. Direct conflict within the same section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard indemnity with three enumerated triggers; "any violation of this Agreement by You" is broad but not ambiguous, and the indemnitee list is spelled out. "[H]arm You may have caused to another" in (c) is the loosest phrase but is tied to intentional or willful conduct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the liquidated damages regime in Section 27 and the indemnity of the Released Parties in Section 25 without contradiction, and survives under Section 31. Checked, no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Liability is triggered only "if it becomes necessary for Angie's List to pursue legal action to enforce" the Agreement, a condition that could be read as a precondition to any liquidated damages at all or as mere preamble. That trigger is genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The section introduces sums that must be read against Section 25's damages architecture and Section 16's remedies paragraph ("if damages are ascertainable, seeking damages"), and its subsection (d) then reverts to actual damages. Some tension but nothing squarely contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[E]ach item of Content posted in violation of this Agreement" leaves the counting unit undefined — a review, a sentence, a photograph — and "in violation of this Agreement" imports the whole of Section 16's open-ended standards. A fixed sum multiplied by an undefined unit is a real construction problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on Section 16's conduct covenants, several of which are subjective, and on the Section 27 trigger requiring legal action. Dependency rather than contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence ends without a full stop and again turns on "each item of Content", an undefined unit, following a list of verbs closed by "exploit for any purpose" — a catch-all against enumerated specifics. Namable list-scope and mechanical defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Section 9's licence restriction and Section 16(P), which use slightly different verb lists, so which conduct triggers the $1,000 is not fixed by one provision alone. Modest relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[E]ach review or record that is aggregated, disrupted, damaged or otherwise affected" ends in an unbounded catch-all ("otherwise affected"), and the damages unit is again indeterminate. That is exactly an ejusdem generis question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 16(G) and (H) but adds "aggregate records or reviews", a use those subsections do not squarely prohibit. Slight mismatch, no outright conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It cross-refers to "the foregoing subsections (a) through (c)" when the subsections are lettered (A) through (C), and it is itself lettered (d) among capitals — a mechanical mismatch in a remedies provision. "[T]o the extent such actual damages can be reasonably calculated" is also an undefined limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement" is asserted for equitable relief, which sits against Section 16's separate injunctive-relief paragraph and Section 25's limitations, though the two can be read together. A modest fit issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he earlier of the verification of delivery or two (2) business days after being sent" is precise, and the permitted channels are enumerated. Little intrinsic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deemed-delivery rule sits against the cancellation provision, which requires the request to be "received" by 5:00 p.m. on the business day before renewal, and the addresses given in the two provisions differ slightly. A specific but small conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital of the statutory DMCA notification elements, expressed as "substantially the following" with a numbered list; the content is dictated by statute and is administrable. Low risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies the copyright regime to "trademark" claims as well, which the DMCA does not cover, but nothing else in the instrument contradicts it. Checked against Section 23 (Copyright Materials); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he entire agreement" and "the subject matter contained in this Agreement" are the classic terms whose scope is fought over, and the warranty that third-party agreements "do not interfere with Your obligations" is a vague, one-sided undertaking. In a dispute over pre-contract representations this clause is the battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against the preamble, which binds the member to "all of the terms and conditions in, and linked to, this Membership Agreement" and to "separate terms and conditions, agreements and privacy policies", and against Section 5's privacy policy — so whether the linked documents are inside or outside the integration is unresolved. A named, specific tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[E]xclusive jurisdiction" in Marion County is immediately undercut by an exception allowing Angie's List alone to sue elsewhere, a one-sided drafting that a court would construe against its drafter, and "where You can be found" is undefined. The contractual one-year limitation period is a further term whose reach (statutory claims?) is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 32's severability sentence and Section 31's survival list, and the exclusive-forum promise is hard to square with Angie's List's reserved election; no other provision resolves the mismatch. Some relational strain, mostly intrinsic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ertain provisions ... including, but not limited to, Sections 12, 14, 15, 17 and 23 through 31" is a textbook general-vs-specific defect: an enumerated list expressly made non-exhaustive, so no one can tell which other provisions survive. That is the clearest expressio unius / catch-all problem in the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The list omits Section 32, which contains the third-party-beneficiary provision on which Section 25's Released Parties depend, and omits Section 9's licence restriction, so survival of key post-termination rights is left open. A specific, checkable incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The severability sentence is unusually drafted — a court "should incorporate a similar provision that would be considered valid" — which is a reformation direction of uncertain effect rather than ordinary severance. "[S]imilar provision" cannot be applied from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its third-party-beneficiary sentence depends on the "Released Parties" defined in Section 25, yet Section 32 is not among the sections listed as surviving termination in Section 31. That is a locatable mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short assent-by-use statement in plain terms; "BY USING THE SERVICE" is definite in meaning even if its legal effect on formation is debatable. Little textual ambiguity within the sentence itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bases assent on use, while the preamble bases it on acceptance ("BY ACCEPTING THE TERMS ... JUST AS IF YOU HAD SIGNED") and Section 19 makes continued use "conclusive acceptance" of modifications; the three formation mechanics are not identical. Mild but genuine friction.
